lines.japanese: だだっ広い駅舎から飛びだして、見えない太陽の下で深呼吸した。
lines.english: I burst from the cavernous station and drew a deep breath beneath the invisible sun.

lines.japanese: 澄んでいるとは言えない都会の濁った大気でも、異物感のわだかまった喉をすすぐには充分だ。
lines.english: The city’s murky air could hardly be called pure, but it was enough to clear the feeling of something caught in my throat.

lines.japanese: 僕は肩で息をしながら、よろめくように歩道橋の階段をのぼった。
lines.english: Breathing hard, I climbed the pedestrian bridge with an unsteady gait.

lines.japanese: １２月の白い空に少しだけ近付いた。
lines.english: I drew a little nearer to December’s white sky.

lines.japanese: ここは柳木原西口の大きな交差点をまたぐ、四方型の歩道橋。
lines.english: This four-way pedestrian bridge spanned the great intersection outside Yanagihara’s west exit.

lines.japanese: 眼下には交差点を行きかう車列。頭上には高速道路を疾走する轟音。
lines.english: Below, columns of cars crossed the junction. Overhead, the expressway thundered.

lines.japanese: そのあいだをくぐり抜けて対角線上の階段を下りれば、そこには背の高い洗練されたビジネスビルが立ちならぶ、静かなオフィス街が広がっている。
lines.english: Beyond them, down the stairs at the opposite corner, spread a quiet office district lined with tall, elegant business towers.

lines.japanese: 柳木原を大別すれば、東が繁華街・西がビジネスタウンになっている。
lines.english: Broadly speaking, eastern Yanagihara was the entertainment district and western Yanagihara the business district.

lines.japanese: 美空学園があるのは西側。
lines.english: Misora Academy stood on the western side.

lines.japanese: 進学校としてそこそこ名の通った僕らの学び舎は、息づまるコンクリートの海、その岸辺にそびえていた。
lines.english: Our school, reasonably well known for sending students on to good universities, towered at the edge of that suffocating concrete sea.
…Oh.

lines.japanese: 反対側のデッキから、僕と同じ階段を目指して歩いてくる彼女の姿を見つけてしまった。
lines.english: On the opposite deck, I had spotted her walking toward the same staircase as me.

lines.japanese: 違うクラスの女子ふたりと並んで、静かな朝に華やいだ声と笑顔を振りまいている。
lines.english: She walked between two girls from another class, scattering bright voices and smiles through the quiet morning.

lines.japanese: いつか森里君たちが言っていたように、渡来さんは否応なく場の空気を変えてしまう存在感をたしかに放っていた。それが天賦の才なのか、後天的な努力によって勝ちえたものなのかは知らないけれど。
lines.english: As Morisato and the others had once said, Watarai carried something that changed the atmosphere around her whether anyone wished it or not. I could not say whether it was an inborn gift or something she had cultivated through effort.

lines.japanese: 彼女たちの後ろから走ってきた二年生の男子が、追い越しざまに体育会系の挨拶を投げていった。渡来さんは握りこぶしを掲げて、陽気に同じ言葉を返す。
lines.english: A second-year boy came running up behind them and tossed out a hearty athlete’s greeting as he passed. Watarai raised a fist and cheerfully returned it in kind.

lines.japanese: 僕はその場で、とっさに欄干の外へ顔を背けた。同時に歩幅も、不自然さで逆に注意を引いてしまわないぐらいにまで落とした。
lines.english: I immediately turned my face beyond the railing. At the same time, I shortened my stride—but only enough that the unnatural motion would not itself attract attention.

lines.japanese: 真下の交差点では、右折の出足の遅れた軽自動車が、後続の気短かな２ドアスポーツから激しいクラクションを浴びせられていた。
lines.english: In the intersection directly below, a compact car had been slow to begin its right turn and was being savaged by the horn of an impatient two-door sports car behind it.

lines.japanese: その後おそるおそる視線を水平に戻すと、あの柔らかな長い髪が階段に差しかかって沈んでいくところだった。
lines.english: When I timidly brought my gaze level again, that soft, long hair was sinking from view as she began down the stairs.

lines.japanese: 僕は深い息をついて、少しだけ速度を戻した。
lines.english: I let out a deep breath and restored a little of my speed.

lines.japanese: ひとにはそれぞれ相応の歩き方がある。それを弁えていないと、僕らは誰かに警笛を鳴らされてしまう。
lines.english: Each person has a proper way of walking through the world. Forget it, and someone will sound a warning horn at you.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: この地上八階建ての近代的なビルディングが、私立美空学園の校舎。
lines.english: This modern eight-story building was my school, the private Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: 頭上高くそびえる都会的な威容は、こうして一流企業のしゃれたビジネスビル群と肩を並べていてもまるで違和感が湧かない。
lines.english: Its urban grandeur towered overhead, entirely at home among the stylish offices of first-rate corporations.

lines.japanese: うん。見た目はいいよね。
lines.english: Yes. It looked good.

lines.japanese: 三年前、入学希望者向けの説明会で初めてこのビル校舎を見上げたときは、パンフレットの謳う“アーバンスタイリッシュなスクールライフ”とやらに青い羨望を覚えたものだ。あのころ僕は若かった。
lines.english: Three years ago, when I first looked up at this vertical campus during an admissions presentation, the brochure’s promise of an “urban, stylish school life” filled me with callow envy. I was young then.

lines.japanese: べつに自分の選んだ進路を後悔してはいないけど、あのときパンフレットで目星を付けた、学食のチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食を味わえないまま終わりそうなのはちょっと残念だ。
lines.english: I did not regret the course I had chosen. Still, it was a little sad to think I might never get to try the cafeteria’s sautéed chicken and fried shrimp meal—the one that had caught my eye in the brochure.

lines.japanese: 歩道橋を降りてから校門へ向かうまでのあいだに、僕はポケットから携帯電話を取りだして時刻を確認した。予鈴まで、あと十分ぐらいある。
lines.english: Between descending the pedestrian bridge and reaching the school gates, I took out my cell phone and checked the time. There were still around ten minutes before the warning bell.

lines.japanese: 今朝はいろいろあったから、もっと切羽詰まった時間だと思ってた。ちょっと安心。これならテスト直前の最終チェックがある程度できそうだ。
lines.english: After all that had happened this morning, I had expected it to be much later. What a relief. I should have time for a reasonable last-minute review before the exam.

lines.japanese: 「え～、なんでぇ～？」
lines.english: “What? Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、知らねってゆってんじゃん！」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, I don’t know!”

lines.japanese: 僕と同じクラスの女子ふたりが歩道橋から下りてきた。周囲を気遣わない、ひどく大きな声で話している。
lines.english: Two girls from my class came down from the pedestrian bridge, talking in remarkably loud voices without a thought for anyone around them.

lines.japanese: ひとりと一瞬目が合ったけど、僕らはお互いに気付かなかったふりをして歩きつづけた。顔ぐらいは知ってるけど一度も話したことがない同級生っていうのは、ふと冷静に考えるとちょっと特殊な関係だなって思う。
lines.english: My eyes met one girl’s for an instant, but we both pretended not to notice and kept walking. When you stopped to think about it, a classmate whose face you knew but to whom you had never once spoken was a peculiar kind of relationship.

lines.japanese: 「なに、そんじゃ、だっちーは来てなかったの？」
lines.english: “Wait, so Datchi wasn’t there?”

lines.japanese: 「だってあいつはスタジオじゃん」
lines.english: “She was in the studio, wasn’t she?”

lines.japanese: 「てかさぁ、だっちー、なんかムネ嘘くさくな～い？」
lines.english: “Speaking of Datchi, don’t her boobs look kinda fake?”

lines.japanese: 「アそそそ、あれチョー固そーなん、ぜってありえんしー、あんな！」
lines.english: “Yes! Totally! Those things look way too firm. No way they’re real.”

lines.japanese: 彼女たちがサンテレビの足立アナについて話しているのだとしたら、今朝のあの情報番組が発端かもしれない。べつに聞きたいわけじゃないけど、勝手に耳へ飛びこんでくる。
lines.english: If they were talking about Adachi, the Sun Television announcer, this morning’s program might have started it. I had no desire to listen, but their words flew into my ears uninvited.

lines.japanese: 「エそんでそんで？　ヤバイじゃんソレ、だってテレビとか来るって、マジかなりでかいケンカでしょ？」
lines.english: “So then what? That’s crazy. If television crews came out, it must’ve been a seriously huge fight, right?”

lines.japanese: やっぱり。グローヴ街の少年乱闘事件は、柳木原のヤングエイジなら誰だって気になって当然のトピックだ。
lines.english: Just as I thought. The Grove Street brawl was naturally a subject of interest to every teenager in Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「知んない。だってなんか、乱闘とかゆってるわりに、病院運ばれたのひとりだけとか言っててー」
lines.english: “Dunno. They’re calling it a brawl, but apparently only one person went to the hospital.”

lines.japanese: 「エじゃあ、他みんなバックレ？　ちょ、不良軍団めっさ野放しじゃん。やァも、このへん超サファリ～」
lines.english: “Then everyone else split? There’s, like, a whole delinquent army running loose. God, this neighborhood’s a total safari.”

lines.japanese: 「てゆか、だって、ここんとこ増えてんらー、そゆアレ。なんかヤンキー同士の小競り合いみたいなン」
lines.english: “I mean, that kinda thing’s been happening more lately, right? Little turf wars between punks and stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「エうっそ、アレ？　テメどこ校だコラァみたいの？　やー何それ何それ、ツッパリじゃん！　かっけぇー、ちょーウケるんですけど」
lines.english: “No way. Like, ‘What school you from, asshole?’ Oh my God, real old-school delinquents! That’s amazing. I’m gonna die laughing.”

lines.japanese: 「やーっべ、うちらも襲われっかも！　きゃはは、貞操帯しとこっかあ！」
lines.english: “Crap, maybe they’ll attack us next! Ah ha ha! Should we buy chastity belts?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。いいじゃんあんた、ピル飲んでんだから」
lines.english: “Why would you need one? You’re on the pill.”

lines.japanese: 「デキなきゃいいのかよ！　てか、誰かうちのノブにゆえよゴム付けろって、超ムカつくわモォー」
lines.english: “So it’s fine as long as I don’t get pregnant? Someone tell my Nobu to wear a condom. God, he pisses me off.”

lines.japanese: 僕ははしゃぐ女子たちの斜め前を歩いていた。どうしてあんなに大きな声で喋るんだろう。
lines.english: I walked diagonally ahead of the excited girls. Why did they have to speak so loudly?

lines.japanese: ポケットの中で携帯電話の輪郭をなぞりながら、やっぱりさっきメモ帳に打ちこんだ一行を消そうかと考えていた。
lines.english: Tracing the outline of my cell phone through my pocket, I wondered again whether I should delete the line I had just entered in its notepad.

lines.japanese: 「あれー？　ね、そいや、さっきあんた言ってた、極秘情報ってなによ？」
lines.english: “Oh, hey. What was that top-secret information you mentioned before?”

lines.japanese: 「あー。あんねー？　あン、マー子に聞いたんだけどー。なんかその乱闘事件に、うちの男子が関わってるかも的な話あるらしくってー」
lines.english: “Oh, right. So, I heard from Mako that there’s this rumor some boys from our school might’ve been involved in the brawl.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なになに関わってるって。うそ、うちにいたのツッパリ系！　ぎゃああ、マジで、やだキモぉ～！」
lines.english: “What do you mean, involved? Wait, we have delinquent types at our school? Oh my God, seriously? Gross!”

lines.japanese: 「なー？　や、知んねーけど、いるとすりゃ９０％セントヘレナのヤツだし。だっせー。つか、だっせー」
lines.english: “Right? I mean, I dunno, but if we do, there’s a ninety-percent chance he’s from Saint Helena. Lame. Just completely lame.”

lines.japanese: ダサいキモいを連呼して、ふたりは僕の後ろでげらげら笑う。
lines.english: Lame and gross, they repeated, cackling behind me.

lines.japanese: セントヘレナは、ワーテルローの戦いに敗れたナポレオン１世が、ウィーン会議によって送られた絶海の孤島。僕らが入学する前からあった特別強化学級の俗称だけど、趣味の悪い冗談だと思う。
lines.english: Saint Helena was the remote island to which the Congress of Vienna had sent Napoleon I after his defeat at Waterloo. It was also the popular name for the special remedial class that had existed since before we entered the school. I thought it a joke in very poor taste.

lines.japanese: 美空学園には、二年間の成績が芳しくなかった生徒を、三年次でひとところにまとめる規定があった。
lines.english: Misora Academy had a rule that gathered students whose grades had been poor for two years into a single class for their third.

lines.japanese: 内外から反対の声もあるそうだけど、実際に厳しい強化措置を受けて飛躍的に成績を上げる生徒も（中には）いるということで、一概に悪習とも言いきれないらしい。
lines.english: There were reportedly objections both within and outside the school. But some students—some—did improve dramatically under its strict remedial measures, so apparently the custom could not be condemned outright.

lines.japanese: 「ってんから、今日ガッコ休んでるヤツいたらソイツとか、ちょー、怪しンじゃね？　つって」
lines.english: “So, like, if anyone’s off school today, that’d be super suspicious, right? That’s what I’m saying.”

lines.japanese: 「へー、マジだー。え、ちなみにその話、だれ情報？」
lines.english: “Oh, totally. Wait, who’d you hear this from?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、マー子だッつってんじゃん」
lines.english: “I just told you. Mako.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、マー子は誰に聞いたんだよ」
lines.english: “I mean, who did Mako hear it from?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねーよ、私はマー子かっつうの」
lines.english: “How should I know? Do I look like Mako?”

lines.japanese: 「ハアー？　何ソレ意味わかんない、ちょ、マー子呼んできてよォ」
lines.english: “What? That makes no sense. Go get Mako.”

lines.japanese: 「無理無理。アイツいま親と喧嘩しててー。ここんとこ彼氏の家に逃げこんでんらー」
lines.english: “No chance. She’s fighting with her parents and crashing at her boyfriend’s place lately.”

lines.japanese: 「うーっそ、あいつ何度目だよプチ家出。マジどんだけだもー」
lines.english: “No way. How many times has she pulled this little runaway act now? Seriously, what is wrong with her?”

lines.japanese: 脱線の多い会話と同じで、彼女たちの歩みはとても緩やかだ。ふたりと友達でも何でもない僕は、それ以上ペースを合わせていることが不可能になった。
lines.english: Like their conversation, forever wandering off course, the girls’ progress was remarkably slow. I was not their friend or anything else, and could no longer contrive to match their pace.

lines.japanese: やけに重い扉をひとりで押して、美空学園の正面玄関から空調の利いた昇降口へ踏みこむ。
lines.english: Alone, I pushed through the oddly heavy door of Misora Academy’s main entrance and stepped into the climate-controlled shoe-locker hall.

lines.japanese: ガラス張りの外壁が太陽光を通すエントランスは、今日も清潔なくせに埃のにおいが満ちていた。
lines.english: Sunlight entered through the glass outer walls. As always, the entrance was immaculate and filled with the smell of dust.
